_note: Flow resources: produced and consumed continuously, delivered by a network, cannot be stockpiled. Failure is instant and cascading. Water is a hybrid — piped like a flow, buffered like a stock, which is why it carries both a network and a bufferedIn.

flows.name: Power
flows.description: Made by the main generator from fuel and carried by the junctions. Every lit room draws on it; when there isn't enough, the priority ladder decides who goes dark.

quote.text: Amber means it's on. If you can read this, thank a stoker.

flows._note: When supply < demand the ladder browns out low-priority buildings first. See catalog/infrastructure/networks.json.

flows.name: Air quality
flows.description: How breathable a level is. Scrubbers and oxygen gardens clean it; crowds and depth foul it, and stale air pools where the ducts don't reach.

quote.text: If you can smell your neighbour's dinner, the scrubber's fine. If you can smell your neighbour, it isn't.

flows._note: Tracked PER LEVEL, not globally — stale air pools in pockets the scrubbers do not reach. This is the whole point of the air system.

flows.name: Water
flows.description: Pumped from deep below, reclaimed from greywater and held in cisterns. People drink it, suites wash in it, and the gardens drink more than anyone.

quote.text: Every drop in this Shaft has been through at least four people. Two of them were probably you.

flows._note: Hybrid. Sourced at the bottom, lifted upward at a power cost proportional to lift height; greywater returns downward free by gravity.
